Assessment
77-year-old female (MRN SYN-0870650) status post second hospitalization this year for melena from bleeding jejunal angioectasias treated via push enteroscopy with argon plasma coagulation (APC), complicated by severe iron deficiency anemia (admission Hb 7.2 g/dL, transfused 3u pRBC; discharge Hb 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 8 ng/mL). Physical exam at discharge noted a 3/6 late-peaking systolic murmur at the RUSB, and review of scanned outside transthoracic echocardiogram (2023-07-12) demonstrates severe calcific aortic stenosis (peak velocity 4.3 m/s, mean gradient 46 mmHg, AVA 0.8 cm2, LVEF 60%). She now reports exertional fatigue and reduced exercise tolerance (stopping when walking to the mailbox). The combination of severe aortic stenosis and recurrent GI bleeding from small-bowel angioectasias represents Heyde syndrome, driven by high-shear-stress proteolysis of high-molecular-weight von Willebrand factor (vWF) multimers across the stenotic aortic valve (acquired von Willebrand syndrome type 2A).
